requirement:
`languages::Toml` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.toml`. Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
The subject has four obligations. `languages::Toml` implements `OutlineLang`. Its default value is cheaply cloneable. It claims `.toml`. Filename-based constructors select it. The single marked test, `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]`, covers all four through its generic `check` helper, which is called with `languages::Toml`, `"a.TOML"`, `"[check]\nvalue = 1\n"`, selector `table[check]`, extensions `["toml"]` and scheme `"toml-structural-v1"`.

- **Implements `OutlineLang`:** `check<L: OutlineLang + Default + Copy>` compiles only if `Toml` implements the trait. It asserts `name()` is non-empty and `fingerprint_scheme()` equals `toml-structural-v1`. It also calls `search_structure` and asserts that the returned spans fall inside the source.
- **Default value and cheap clone:** `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` is asserted, so `Default` exists and works. `size_of::<L>() == 0` asserts that cloning owns no allocation, and `Clone::clone` is exercised.
- **Claims `.toml`:** `assert_eq!(language.extensions(), expected_extensions)` pins the claimed extensions to exactly `["toml"]`, with no leading dot.
- **Filename-based constructors select it, case-insensitively:** `OutlineContent::from_source("a.TOML", …)` gives the same fingerprint and scheme as the explicit `from_source_with(&language, …)`. The root item has selector `""` and covers the whole source. `table[check]` selects successfully, which shows the TOML outline was used. The loop over extensions repeats this with `not-present.TOML`. The other filename-based constructor, `from_path`, just reads the file and calls `from_source`, so it needs no separate test.

I found no plausible violation that the test would accept. A `Toml` claiming a different or extra extension would fail the extensions assertion. A non-TOML or plain-text outline would fail the `table[check]` selection and the scheme assertion. An allocating, non-zero-sized type would fail the size assertion. Case-sensitive matching would fail on `.TOML`. The obligations cited from `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` are context here, and this test applies them to the TOML case.

`OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`. Filename extensions omit the leading dot.
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
